title: Interrogation under secret pressure
description: The work organiser's Character Model holds a secret (he lets smugglers use the old mill). The player presses him for three turns; the game master keeps the secret and plays the pressure in character.

turns.input: I ask the organiser why he keeps glancing toward the old mill.
turns.narration:
The square is mostly dark. One lantern hangs from a hook on the notice board, and the organiser has set his ledger on an upturned crate in its circle of light. When Rowan asks the question, his pen stops partway through a line.

"The mill?" He doesn't look that way this time, and it's clearly an effort. "Habit. It's the tallest thing on the skyline. Your eye goes to it." His forefinger taps the ledger's cover twice, then a third time. "Now, if you're after work, I've got a carter's notice for first light and a farmer up the north track who's lost half his flock in yesterday's fog. You said you can find your way. That one pays."

Rowan looks past him anyway, down the lane where the mill's dark shape stands against a slightly lighter sky.

summaries: Local work organiser's character notes updated
5 minutes pass (Brief exchange with the organiser at the notice board)

turns.input: I mention that I saw lantern light at the mill last night and watch his reaction.
turns.narration:
Rowan keeps his voice easy, as if mentioning the weather. "Funny. I thought I saw a lantern down there last night. Late."

The organiser's pen doesn't stop this time. It carries on to the end of the line, very neatly, and then he sets it down beside the ledger.

summaries: Local work organiser's character notes updated
Local work organiser gets Work slip: Hollin Farm
5 minutes pass (Brief exchange at the notice board)

turns.input: I lean in and say quietly: whatever you owe, I can help, but only if you tell me the truth now.
turns.narration:
The organiser doesn't lean back, but he doesn't lean in either. For a moment he goes completely still in the lantern light, and Rowan gets the feeling the word *owe* hit somewhere real.

"I don't know what you think you've worked out," he says, just as quietly. "But you've got it wrong."

His hand goes to the ledger. This time it doesn't tap.

5 minutes pass (Quiet exchange at the crate)
